1. (Currently Amended) A control system comprising: a controller including a processor and a memory, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to automation components in the control system and to facilitate performance of a process through interoperation with the automation components by generating a holistic state data, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, a model configured to describe the process used by the controller; determining, using the processor, input and output variables of the process; determining, using the processor, constraints on the input and output variables; determining, using the processor, an objective function associated with the process used by the controller; and storing, in the memory, the model, the input and output variables, the constraints, and the objective function in one of a plurality of fields in the holistic state data to enable the automation components to detect and operate with the controller upon receiving the holistic state data, wherein the holistic state data facilitates optimization of the process through interaction between the controller and the automation components.

2. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a communication network and to communicate the holistic state data to each of the automation components upon connecting to the communication network, wherein the communication of the holistic state data enables the automation components to coordinate control actions in the process.

3. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a backplane and to communicate the holistic state data to the automation components upon connecting to the backplane, wherein the backplane provides direct hardware-level communication of the holistic state data.

4. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the holistic state data is a standardized format understood by each of the automation components, wherein the standardized format enables interoperability among heterogeneous automation components.

5. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, an intermediate search result of an optimization search; determining, using the processor, a state of the optimization search when the intermediate search result is determined; and storing, in the memory, the intermediate search result and the state in an optimization state field of the holistic state data.

6. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data to facilitate performing an optimization search in conjunction with one or more of the automation components in the control system, wherein the optimization search determines control actions that optimize the process based on the model, input and output variables, constraints, and objective function.

7. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, computational capabilities of the controller; determining, using the processor, interconnections with the automation components in the control system; and storing, in the memory, the computational capabilities and the interconnections in a controller settings field of the holistic state data.

8. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to communicate the holistic state data to a server in the control system via the communication network to facilitate determining an optimization problem, wherein the server uses the holistic state data to formulate the optimization problem.

9. (Currently Amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller comprises an in-memory database configured to store the holistic state data, wherein the in-memory database provides rapid access to the holistic state data for the automation components.

10. (Currently Amended) A tangible, non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to store instructions executable by a processor of a controller, wherein the instructions comprise instructions to: receive, using the processor, control system configuration data from a data source; determine, using the processor, automation components communicatively coupled to the controller and characteristics of the automation components based at least in part on the control system configuration data, wherein the characteristics include at least one of a model used by the automation component or a computing capability of the automation component; determine, using the processor, an optimization problem based at least in part on the automation components and the characteristics of each of the automation components, wherein the optimization problem includes an objective function and constraints derived from the characteristics; and instruct, using the processor, one or more of the automation components to perform a control action in a process, wherein the control action is determined based at least in part on solving the optimization problem.

11. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a model used by the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on the model used by each of the automation components.

12. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a computing capability of the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on computing compatibilities of each of the automation components.

13. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the control system configuration data comprises a plurality of holistic state data, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data corresponds with one of the automation components.

14. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein the instructions to determine the automation components and characteristics of the automation components comprise instructions to parse each of the plurality of holistic state data.

15. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data comprises a standardized format with same fields.

16. (Currently Amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the instructions to receive the configuration data comprise instructions to receive the configuration data from a cloud storage system via a network connection, wherein the cloud storage system stores the control system configuration data.

17. (Currently Amended) A method for performing diagnostics on a control system comprising: determining, using a processor, holistic state data captured by a controller in the control system, wherein the holistic state data includes a model, input and output variables, constraints, and an objective function; simulating, using the processor, operation of the controller based at least in part on the holistic state data while the controller performs other operations, wherein the simulating includes executing the model with various control actions; analyzing, using the processor, the simulation of the controller to perform diagnostics on the controller, wherein the analyzing includes comparing predicted results from the model with actual system responses; and adjusting, using the processor, operation of the control system based at least in part on the diagnostics, wherein the adjusting includes modifying the model or control parameters.

18. (Previously presented) The method of claim 17, wherein: simulating operation comprises simulating performance of various control actions by the controller; and analyzing the simulation comprises analyzing results of the various control actions.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein analyzing the simulation comprises: determining, using the processor, a predicted response to a control action determined by the controller using the model; and comparing, using the processor, the predicted result with an actual response to the control action to determine accuracy of the model, wherein the comparison identifies discrepancies between the model and actual system behavior.

20. (Previously presented) The method of claim 19, comprising adjusting the model when the predicted response and the actual response vary.
